_meta.note: Ecological output chain data for C3 photosynthesis. Three analytical layers: ecological outputs (carbon, O2, biomass, sequestration), energy efficiency (quantum yields, stoichiometries), and stress responses (D-C imbalance under four stress states).

1.key_metric: O2 evolution at saturation = 28 µmol m-2 s-1

3.carbon_fixation_contribution: NADPH for Calvin cycle and N/S assimilation
3.biomass_contribution: NADPH drives fatty acid synthesis and chlorophyll biosynthesis beyond carbon fixation

4.carbon_fixation_contribution: ATP for Calvin cycle RuBP regeneration

5.o2_evolution: indirect (O2 consumed by photorespiration = ~5 µmol m-2 s-1)
5.biomass_contribution: direct: fixed carbon enters all biosynthetic pathways
5.key_metric: Net An = 20 µmol CO2 m-2 s-1; Photorespiration loss ~25%

6.carbon_fixation_contribution: converts fixed CO2 to organic carbon (G3P)
6.biomass_contribution: G3P is universal precursor to all plant organic compounds
6.key_metric: G3P export ~4 µmol triose-P m-2 s-1

7.carbon_fixation_contribution: distributes fixed carbon to growth sinks
7.biomass_contribution: sucrose and starch fuel all plant growth; sink demand determines whole-plant carbon balance
7.key_metric: Export efficiency ~75% of fixed C; sucrose ~12 + starch ~6 µmol C m-2 s-1

0.notes: Near-theoretical: energy transfer within LHCII is 95%+ efficient via Forster resonance transfer.

1.stoichiometry: 4 photons -> 1 O2; 2 PQH2; 4 H+ into lumen
1.notes: Fv/Fm = 0.83 in healthy dark-adapted leaf vs theoretical max 0.88. Dark reactions and charge recombination cause the gap.

2.stoichiometry: 2 H+ pumped per electron via Q-cycle at cytochrome b6f
2.notes: Highly efficient electron carrier. Q-cycle amplifies proton pumping. Rate-limiting but energetically efficient.

3.notes: Y(I) ~0.80 under moderate light. Losses from acceptor-side limitation and P700+ recombination.

4.stoichiometry: 14/3 H+ per ATP (spinach CF1CF0); ATP/NADPH ratio 1.28 vs demand 1.5
4.notes: ATP/NADPH mismatch requires ~15% cyclic electron flow supplement. Thermodynamically efficient (~60%) under in vivo pmf.

5.stoichiometry: 8 photons minimum per CO2 fixed (theoretical); ~18 photons actual (C3 with photorespiration)
5.notes: Largest efficiency gap in the system. Theoretical minimum 8 photons/CO2; actual ~16-18 due to photorespiration ATP/NADPH costs. The 11% theoretical vs 6% practical whole-chain efficiency gap originates here.

6.stoichiometry: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH consumed per CO2 fixed; essentially 100% of G3P produced goes toward RuBP regeneration or export
6.notes: Highly efficient when ATP and NADPH supply is adequate. TPU limitation under high CO2 is the efficiency failure mode.

7.stoichiometry: ~75% of fixed carbon exported; ~25% consumed by leaf respiration and photorespiratory carbon skeleton recycling
7.notes: Export efficiency highly variable by species, age, and temperature. The 25% respiratory cost is largely unavoidable maintenance.

0.effect: NPQ increases to dissipate excess excitation energy

1.effect: Mn4CaO5 cluster destabilization; D1 protein damage rate accelerates; Fv/Fm declines
1.direction: D increases sharply (repair demand exceeds repair rate)

4.effect: Membrane fluidity increases; H+ leak across thylakoid rises; ATP synthesis efficiency drops
4.direction: C decreases (ATP yield per H+ declines)

5.effect: Rubisco specificity factor Sc/o decreases with temperature; photorespiration fraction increases sharply above 30°C

4.effect: Membrane dehydration increases passive H+ conductance; pmf destabilized

5.effect: Stomatal closure reduces CO2 supply; internal CO2/O2 ratio falls; photorespiration increases; Rubisco activation state declines
5.direction: D increases sharply (substrate limitation + O2 competition)

7.effect: Reduced turgor limits phloem loading; sucrose export declines; starch accumulation inhibits upstream phases via Pi trapping

high_light.description: Excess light (PAR > 1000 µmol photons m-2 s-1)

0.effect: NPQ (non-photochemical quenching) activated; thermal dissipation increases; effective antenna size decreases to protect PSII
0.severity: moderate (protective, not damaging if NPQ functions)

1.effect: PSII photoinhibition when excitation exceeds repair capacity; D1 protein oxidized; Fv/Fm declines; O2 evolution rate falls
1.direction: D increases (repair demand exceeds capacity at D-C balance of Phase 3 Lifecycle)

3.effect: PSI acceptor-side limitation under fluctuating light; reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated at FeS clusters under sudden high light pulses
3.direction: C decreases (NADPH production impaired by acceptor limitation)
3.severity: moderate to severe under rapid fluctuation

elevated_co2.description: Elevated atmospheric CO2 (>700 ppm, e.g. 2×CO2 scenarios)

5.effect: Rubisco carboxylation rate increases; oxygenation ratio Vo/Vc decreases; photorespiration suppressed; An increases by ~20-30%
5.direction: D decreases (CO2 substrate limitation relieved; O2 competition reduced)

6.effect: Increased G3P production; ATP and NADPH consumed faster; cyclic electron flow demand increases
6.direction: D increases slightly (energetic demand on light reactions increases)

7.effect: TPU (triose phosphate utilization) limitation emerges when sucrose and starch synthesis cannot keep up with increased G3P supply; feedback inhibits upstream An
7.severity: moderate (observed as CO2 response curve saturation at elevated CO2 under cold or nutrient limitation)
